bindings.title: Import "lib: Research Specialist" and select it on Research Specialist (Sub-workflow)
bindings.detail: This template calls a separate workflow named lib: Research Specialist, and it is included in your download as lib/lib-research-specialist.json. Import that file into n8n first (Workflows -> Import from File), then open Research Specialist (Sub-workflow) and pick it in the workflowId selector. The selector is empty until you do: a workflow id only exists inside your own instance, so it cannot be set for you.

bindings.title: Select the Google Sheets documentId
bindings.detail: The dropdown shows "Document Tracker", which is a placeholder label with no value behind it - the node looks configured and is not. Open each of: Append Audit Row (Google Sheets), Load Previous Snapshot, Park in Dead-Letter Queue, Persist Deliverable to Google Sheets and pick the real documentId from the list.

behaviour.title: Point the HTTP calls at your own endpoint
behaviour.detail: The URL "enrichment.example.com" is illustrative - example.com is reserved for documentation and resolves to nothing useful. Replace it with the service you are actually calling, and set that service's authentication on the node.

behaviour.title: Clear the pinned sample data before going live
behaviour.detail: "Receive Inbound Webhook" carries pinned sample data, which is what lets the workflow run end to end before you have wired anything up. While it is pinned, a manual execution reads the sample and never calls the real service - so the run succeeds and proves nothing about your setup. Unpin it once the credentials and bindings are in place.
